A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LBC research work. All 18 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, references, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-bandit simulations, MovieLens and Yahoo! evaluations, and appendix experiments comparing arm-selection strategies.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and real-data experiments, including expanded baseline comparisons and appendix evaluations under different reward-noise levels.

M1.justification: The specified confidence radius used by the ellipsoid separation test changes from the time/dimension/regularization expression in v1 Equation (1) to the determinant-based expression in v2 Equations (1)–(2). Neighbor-based observation sharing, LinUCB arm selection, and graph-edge removal remain substantially unchanged. The new computational implementation description alone does not establish another algorithm change.

E1.justification: MovieLens, Yahoo!, and the angular and Gaussian synthetic bandit families are retained. v2 Appendix A.10 introduces reward-noise scenarios with sigma = 0.5 and 2.0, beyond v1's unit-noise Gaussian evaluation. Changes in cluster counts are experimental configurations rather than new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated SCLUB and CMLB comparisons across synthetic and real-data benchmarks. v1's corresponding comparisons contain DynUCB and CLUB alongside Ind and, where available, Oracle. SCLUB's underlying paper was already cited in v1, but the algorithm was not included in those experiments.

E3.justification: The stated alpha search expands from [0.05, 3.0] to [0.05, 5.0], and synthetic CLUB thresholds change from {0.1, 1.0} to minimum-gap-based values. Gaussian benchmarks and the arm-policy study replace M = 2 and 4 with M = 6, changing the associated arm counts. v2's real-data legends show DynUCB with M = 5 and 20 despite retained prose specifying 10. Agent counts, horizons, and main feature dimensions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit noise-sensitivity comparison of regret and clustering performance in Appendix A.10. The existing question of whether LinUCB separates ellipsoids effectively is retained, with the Uniform/GreedyLBC comparison revised from two- and four-cluster configurations to six clusters. Alpha-sensitivity analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over 20 runs. However, v1's standard-deviation bands disappear from v2's main and appendix line plots, substantially reducing uncertainty reporting across the empirical evidence. Figure 4 retains standard-deviation error bars. This does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v2 adds SCLUB/CMLB results and revises existing curves and bars. For example, Yahoo! LBC regret is approximately 11–12 thousand in v1 Figure 4 versus 6–8 thousand in v2 Figure 4; revised tuning prevents interpreting this as an isolated same-setting gain. The angular M = 6 clustering results from v1 Figure 3 are omitted, while Gaussian results are replaced with M = 6 noise comparisons showing incomplete clustering recovery.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the two-cluster sample-complexity bound and proof, adds Lemma 2 on expected incorrectly included neighbors, and substantially rewrites Theorem 1 and its appendix proof. The regret analysis changes from the Gaussian-noise/cyclic-agent formulation to synchronous pulling with balanced clusters and a different clustering-error term. Confidence-region and regret definitions also change; these are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claim that ellipsoid-based collaboration improves regret and clustering remain unchanged. v2 Section 3 adds explicit claims of first using an exact ellipsoid separation test and requiring no additional clustering information or parameters, sharpening the claimed novelty and applicability.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting clustering difficulty to arm conditioning, parameter separation, noise, and dimension, and discusses a distinct clustering 'price' in the regret bound. It also qualifies the MovieLens discussion by noting small differences from Ind and interprets the new noise experiments as evidence of robustness.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 describes Cholesky/eigen decompositions, derivatives, Newton minimization, iteration behavior, and computational complexity for the separation test. v2 also discloses 20 Intel Xeon 3.20 GHz CPUs and approximately 18 hours of computation. Dataset preprocessing descriptions largely move from the main text to the appendix rather than being newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ghosh et al. (2022) and the Alger (2021) computational reference, while removing Lai (1987) and Dekel et al. (2010). It adds positioning against CMLB and explicit exact-separation and clustering-parameter contrasts. Most of the dedicated Related Work section relocates material already present in v1.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and reordered around applications. Related Work, Main Contributions, and Paper Organization become separate sections, while synthetic construction and real-data descriptions move into dedicated appendix subsections. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond scientific additions alone.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main text and extensively redraws the plots with vertically stacked panels, revised legends, different colors, and linear rather than logarithmic time axes. The six-cluster angular regret panels move into appendix Figures A.2–A.3. Real-data bars are rearranged and expanded, and appendix figures receive a separate numbering scheme.

improvement.justification: The added baselines and computational details are useful, but v2 removes most uncertainty bands and the angular six-cluster clustering results. Moreover, Appendix A.1's claimed equivalent separation formula disagrees with the main expression: with Ai = Aj = 4, both epsilons = 1, v = 1, and s = 1/2, Equation (3) gives 0 whereas A.1 gives 0.75. This leaves implementation consistency unresolved. These benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
